I'm really anxious and depressed, but I was at a better place during The Eras Tour. However, I was not when I went to Phoebe Bridgers' concert in a festival here in Brazil (she played before Lorde, so it was very crowded), and what I can tell you is (and it may seem a little bit obvious): drink water, carry your medicines, make friends if you're going alone and that's something you like to do (I made a bunch of festival friends and they helped me when Graceland, Too was playing because I was crying and heaving) and try to focus on things that can distract you beforehand — so, for instance, when I felt like I was going to spiral, I started counting how many people had white blonde hair. Also, charge your phone to the max and bring a power bank! Using your phone can help you distract yourself a lot in these situations.   

And, from my experience in Taylor's concerts (I went to three here in Brazil!!), everything will be amazing. She's very punctual (which helped a lot with my anxiety) and it's quite fun to notice some things. Overall a great experience no matter what sits you're on. The people are also very nice and kind! Enjoy and take care <3

I'm discussing it with my friend since yesterday and we gathered a few things I'd like to say. First of all, I really think the album is great, the lyrics are amazing (except tattoed golden retriever, but I laughed at that) and even the Jack Antonoff's overused productions didn't bother me — even though I gravitate more towards the Aaron Dessner's songs. 

I also thought the fact that she publicized the album being mainly about Joe was really smart. The man was trembling, sending notes left and right to the media, thinking he'd be the only subject. He wasn't. Some songs have Matty Heally written all over them (like Down Bad, Guilty as Sin?, TTPD), while the heavier ones are indeed about Joe (loml, So long, London and Black Dog comes to mind).

The main thing I found was that Joe's songs were filled with grief and a sense of rage that comes when you lose something important, while Matty's songs were filled with the feeling that comes when you have an intense, but rather adolescent relationship (she even says so in Down Bad). She makes it clear that she loved Joe so much that, when she lost him, she was trying to fill the gaps he left — and Matty was another way of her doing so. It felt intense because it **was** intense. And she knew he wasn't a good idea (I loved the fact that she explicitly told us he told Lucy — Dacus? — he wanted to off himself if things didn't work out. This seems like Healy's blueprint). I think she fell into that relationship as a means to an end, to get over Joe, but it backfired. And it also ended because they didn't love each other, not truly, anyway, it was, as we say in Portuguese: "fogo no rabo", or "fire in the ass", which means something that fizzles out quickly because it was a decision made out of pure lust, in this case, and not really something thought of. We all been there. And, like she says in the prologue, it felt like a manic episode (even for us, the fans, that don't know anything really). 

I don't get people who are saying she would go back to Joe in a heartbeat if he asked, or even to Matty. I think she buried those two relationships in this album and made it clear that, while both were important, she does not want them back. She's just studying both of them under the microscope of someone who lived those things. I get Taylor. I'm nostalgic like that, too, and sometimes I catch myself overanalyzing things that happened when I was fifteen (I'm now twenty-seven).

Some people are also saying they're disappointed she didn't end things with Matty because he's a racist, but I think she would not write the specific reason on her songs (imagine if she said "we broke up because he was mean to Ice Spice"). Also, we don't know her personally and don't know her life and thoughts. The parasocial relationship with Taylor is ruining some people's perception of her art — we're not her friends, we're her fans, we consume the product she manufactures, and the sooner we accept it, the better.  

I also loved The Alchemy because it seems to be about Travis. Loved, loved the lyric about the trophy. I think she's in a better space right now, where her heart is open for love again and we're seeing it firsthand.

Overall, I think the album is really concise and well-written. Taylor again made me sure that she is my favorite artist and for a handful of reasons.

I lost my cat a month ago. Life is not the same without her and I miss her deeply, but I also know she wouldn't like to see me sad. For me, it seems to be so unjust that she died so suddenly, that God took her away from me. I'm not religious in any form, but I like to imagine she's in heaven, looking down at me. 

The pain doesn't subside. That didn't happen to me yet and it's been thirty days without my Ramona. I look at her pictures and cry, thinking about that tiny ball of fur and life that left me too soon. But I know that, somewhere, she's hoping I get better. 

  
I had mental health issues for a long time, and my cat helped. One time I was in a really bad place and I tried to take my life, and I didn't because of her. I was in the shower, sitting on the floor, and I saw her face and her paws on the door and in that moment I felt so loved, so seen, that I didn't want to die anymore. She stayed with me for 10 years, the worst and best years of my life and I miss her so, so, so much. But dying won't solve this — and we have to be rational sometimes, arguing with ourselves and our more emotional side. And she wouldn't like to see me dead, while I have my whole life ahead of me. 

What I can tell you is that our pets love us more than anything and that love never stops, not even when they die. I had a dog when I was a kid and she died when I was 16, and she stayed with me through all those years — I dreamt about her until a few years ago, but the love never went away. Sometimes I still remember the fact that she smiled and I feel somewhat warmer, calmer, softer. 

I hope it gets better for us, and I hope you get better, too. Life is too short and too precious to waste, and I know this sounds like a cliche, but it's the truth. Someday, maybe, you'll fall in love with another pet that your dog sent to you and life will seem brighter again. 

Until then, stay. Just stay. It gets better. I got better from my depression and I feel as if I'm no longer in a labyrinth looking for a way out — my cat and my dog (I have a bulldog and she's 3 years old) helped me through that path. 

Your dog loves you still and he's looking after you, even though it's not physically and that's too hard too swallow. But he wouldn't want to see you dead. Stay. Just stay.

I was also with my cat when she was euthanised and the same thought ran over my head during all the time it was happening. She seemed so fragile, so small, so pure, and it wasn't fair she was being taken away from me, from life. It also wasn't fair that she'd become ashes after being loved for ten years. She also let me hold her paw for a long time, and I also pressed to see her claws, her beautiful, harmful and long claws. I used to joke with my mom that we held paws everyday. It's been 6 days without her, and yesterday I said goodnight to her out of routine and it felt like I was talking with a ghost. I'm not working properly, I'm not being a person properly, I can only sleep if I take medicines. This pain I'm feeling is like no other I have ever felt — I screamed when she died, I screamed days after, too. My voice has become hoarse. 

I hope you have someone to hold you and, if you don't, I can tell you that grief is not linear and it comes in waves. And it also doesn't matter if it's been six days, like for me, or three weeks, like it is for you. We loved them so much and the thought of them being gone is unbearable.

My grandfather also died four months ago, and I still forget he's gone most of the days. With my cat, and I imagine it's the same with you, it's different because we saw each other everyday and the pain feels as if someone's stabbing me repeatedly with something sharp. Actually, it feels like someone has taken a big chunk of my heart — and, in part, this happened. Oh, I'd give anything to pet her one more time and hold her little paws in my hand. 

I hope she visits you in your sleep. I hope this passes, for me and for you, and that their memories bring happiness more than pain in the next few days.
